Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Town, shops & places

settlement noun

a place where people have settled

also settlements, colony, settler, settlers, found a settlement

classical

Cic. Agr. 2.73: colōniam collocāre idōneīs in locīs (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. colony

colōnia, colōniae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a settlement, a colony

A town founded by settlers sent out from Rome, and the settlers themselves: to found a settlement is colōniam dēdūcere (Cic. Rep. 2.9; M-O). It can also be any dwelling or farm (Lewis & Short). A settler is colōnus, which is also a farmer, a tenant.

Other words

  • sēdēs, sēdis f. — a home, a place to live (of a people)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.31.14: aliud domicilium, aliās sēdēs · Declension on Wiktionary

    A seat, and so the place where a people has settled (Lewis & Short); usually plural in this sense. For a small settlement, a hamlet, see village.

Examples

  • quī cum ūnā domō jam capī nōn possint, in aliās domōs tamquam in colōniās exeunt

    when they can no longer fit in one house, they go out to other houses, like settlers to new coloniesCic. Off. 1.54

  • serpit per colōniam fāma; concurrere omnēs, ipsum puerum tamquam mīrāculum aspicere

    the news creeps through the town; everyone runs together and stares at the boy himself as a wonderPlin. Ep. 9.33.5

  • ut domō ēmigrent, aliud domicilium, aliās sēdēs, remōtās ā Germānīs, petant

    that they should leave home and look for another dwelling, other places to settle, far from the GermansCaes. BG 1.31.14

See also village, town, agreement.
